threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, governance and initial priorities for the initiative.

messages.text: Welcome all to this channel for our Sustainable Housing Portfolio Optimisation Initiative. Over the next 30 days we need a clear scope, success metrics, and a simple way to steer decisions. I will lean on the draft operating model and business case in A2 and the governance ideas in A8 as starting points, linked to T2 and T9. For now, I suggest we focus the first month on three outcomes: 1) a documented scope and success metrics for the first 30 days, 2) a basic governance and decision structure, and 3) a shortlist of early priorities that can show results to the board in the first quarter. Can each of you react here with your top one or two priorities for this first month, and any concerns about scope or governance?

Thanks for kicking this off. From the housing side, my priorities for the first month would be: 1) get a clean view of current occupancy, rent levels and top service issues via T1 so we know where we stand, and 2) agree how decisions will be made day to day so my team knows who to go to for what, which links to T9 and A8. On scope, I would like to confirm whether the first 30 days are mainly about analysis and design, or if you expect us to already start changing processes in buildings. That will affect how we communicate with tenants and staff.

From my side, I see two immediate needs. First, to frame the target operating model and business case under T2, at least at a high level, so we can explain to the board how this initiative will impact revenue, costs and occupancy. Second, to outline the KPI structure that will later feed into T5, even if we only define a small set of metrics for the first 30 days. For governance, I would like clarity on how often we report to you and in what format, so I can align A2 and A8 with your expectations.

On the digital and sustainability side, I would like us to confirm whether the first 30 days include a first cut of the green ICT roadmap under T3, or if that comes after the business case in T2 is more mature. A3 already sketches some ideas, but I need to know how tightly we want to couple ICT decisions to the financial model. Also, for governance, it would help to know if there will be a small working group that can quickly validate ICT related decisions, or if everything goes through the main steering structure in A8.

From a quality and audit perspective, I would like to see two things in scope for the first 30 days. One is a draft of the quality and compliance checklist under T4, based on A4, so we have a common standard before we start pilots. The other is clarity on how findings and non conformities will be escalated within the governance structure in A8. For success metrics, I suggest we include at least one early indicator related to process consistency or audit readiness, not only financial or occupancy metrics.

On your question about scope for the first 30 days: I suggest we focus mainly on analysis and design, with only very light operational tweaks where we see no risk for tenants. That means T1, T2, T3 and T4 are the core work items, and we use them to prepare for more visible changes later. Any process changes that could affect tenants should be piloted only after we have a communication approach in place. Does that framing work for you?

That framing works for me. If we keep changes light in the first month, I can focus my team on getting T1 done properly and feeding you a reliable baseline. I will also start noting any quick wins we see in operations, but I will not roll them out widely until we have the governance and communication pieces in place. For success metrics, I would propose: 1) baseline completed and validated, 2) draft operating model and business case ready for your review, and 3) governance charter agreed and shared. That seems achievable in 30 days.

I like those three metrics. To make them a bit more concrete for T2, I suggest we define success for the first 30 days as having at least a high level view of cost and benefit ranges, even if we do not yet have precise numbers. That will allow us to position A2 with the board as an initial case, with a clear note that detailed figures will follow. For governance under T9, I can draft a simple structure based on A8, with a steering group and a working group, and we can refine it together.

If we agree on those three metrics, I would add a fourth one related to ICT and sustainability, but still light. For example, we could aim to have a prioritised list of green ICT opportunities under T3, with rough impact estimates, even if the full roadmap in A3 is not final. That way, when you present A2, you can already point to digital levers that support the business case. I can work with you to make sure the ICT items are realistic given our current systems.

I support the three metrics and the suggestion to add an ICT related one. I would also like to see a quality element in the first 30 days, even if it is modest. For example, we could commit to having a first draft of the checklist in A4 under T4, and a plan for how we will run baseline audits later. That would give us a clear link between the operating model in A2 and the way we will monitor it in practice.

Let me try to summarise what I hear for the first 30 days. Scope: focus on analysis and design, with T1, T2, T3 and T4 as the main work items, and only minimal operational tweaks that do not affect tenants. Success metrics: 1) baseline of portfolio performance completed and validated, 2) draft operating model and business case ready for my review, 3) governance and decision structure documented and shared, 4) prioritised list of green ICT opportunities, and 5) draft quality and compliance checklist plus a plan for audits. If this reflects our shared view, I would like to record this as our agreed scope and success metrics for the first 30 days.

The summary works for me. On governance, I would just ask that we keep the escalation paths simple so site teams are not confused. As long as A8 and T9 make it clear who decides on operational changes versus strategic ones, I am comfortable.

I am aligned with that summary. For T9, I will take the first pass at translating A8 into a concrete structure for this initiative, including steering and working groups, and some basic reporting expectations. I will share a draft here before we finalise it.

The scope and metrics look good from my side. For governance, I would appreciate if the working group has enough autonomy to move on smaller ICT items without waiting for every steering meeting, as long as we stay within the budget envelope later defined under T10. We can reflect that in A8.

I am also aligned. One request from my side is that the governance in A8 explicitly mentions how audit findings and quality issues will be reported and prioritised. That will help when we later execute T8 and T12. We can keep it light for now, but I would like the principle to be there.

Good. On governance, I propose the following structure, based on A8 and your input. A small steering group with myself and one representative from each area, meeting every two weeks to confirm direction and resolve escalations. A working group that meets weekly and handles day to day coordination across T1, T2, T3 and T4. Operational decisions that affect tenants or staff go through the steering group, while analytical and design work can be approved in the working group. If there are no objections, I will consider this our agreed governance structure and decision rights for this initiative.

No objections from me. The split between steering and working group is clear enough for my teams. Once you confirm the names for each group, I will brief the site managers so they know how to route questions.

Works for me as well. I will reflect this structure in the next version of A2 and in the governance draft for T9, and I will outline the reporting cadence so we are ready for the first steering meeting.

threads.thread_goal: Review housing portfolio baseline and select phase 1 pilot properties.

messages.text: I have uploaded the first cut of the Housing Portfolio Performance Baseline in A1, covering occupancy, rent levels and key service issues per property, as part of T1. I have also drafted an initial shortlist of potential phase 1 pilot properties under T6, based on occupancy gaps, recurring issues, and ease of access for our teams. Before we lock anything, I would like your feedback on both the baseline and the selection criteria. Are there any data points you are missing in A1, and do the proposed criteria make sense for phase 1?

Looking at A1, the occupancy and rent data are clear. For the business case in T2 and later T11, it would help to have an estimate of service cost per unit for at least the candidate pilot properties, even if it is approximate. That would allow us to see where operational improvements could have the biggest financial impact. On the criteria for T6, I like the focus on occupancy gaps and recurring issues, but I would also consider including at least one property that is already performing well, as a reference point.

From an ICT and sustainability angle, A1 gives a good operational picture, but I am missing any indication of current digital usage, such as portal adoption or digital communication rates. Even a rough estimate for the candidate pilots would help me align T3 and T7. For T6, I would suggest we include at least one building where tenants are already somewhat engaged digitally, so we can test green ICT features without starting from zero everywhere.

A1 is a solid start. For quality and audits, I would like to see a simple indicator of incident frequency or severity per property, even if it is just counts of major issues over the last year. That will help when we later run T8 and apply the checklist from A4. For T6, I recommend we include at least one property with known quality issues, so we can test how well our future processes and audits work in a more challenging environment.

Thanks for pulling this together. From a leadership perspective, I want to make sure the phase 1 pilots give us a mix of quick wins and learning opportunities. That means we should not only pick the most problematic buildings, but also some where we can show early improvement in occupancy or tenant satisfaction. When you refine T6, please keep in mind the budget constraints we will set under T10, and try to avoid a list that requires heavy investment in the first quarter.

Good points. I can extend A1 with a simple estimate of service cost per unit for the candidate pilots, using our internal cost allocations. It will not be perfect, but it should be enough for T2 and T11. On the criteria, I like the idea of including a well performing property as a reference. I will add that as a fourth criterion alongside occupancy gaps, recurring issues, and ease of access.

On digital usage, we do not have perfect data, but I can approximate portal adoption and digital communication rates for the candidate pilots based on login stats and email open rates. I will add two columns to A1 for that. For T6, I will make sure at least one of the pilots has relatively high digital engagement, so you can test the green ICT roadmap and communication plan under T3 and T7.

For incidents, we have logs that will feed into A7 later, but I can pull a summary of major issues per property and add that to A1 for the candidate pilots. That should help you plan T8 and T12. I will also flag at least one property with known quality issues in the T6 shortlist, so we can test our future processes in a tougher setting.

Once you update A1 with service cost estimates and the extra criteria, I can use that to refine the financial view in A2 and the efficiency modelling in T11. It would be helpful if you could mark the candidate pilots clearly in A1, so I can focus my analysis there first.

With the digital usage columns in A1, I can map the candidate pilots against the ICT initiatives in A3 and the communication channels in A6. That will help us choose pilots where we can realistically test features like energy monitoring or digital notices in phase 1. Please let me know once A1 is updated so I can adjust T3 and T7 accordingly.

The incident summary will be very useful. When you flag the property with known quality issues in T6, I will start thinking about how to apply the draft checklist from A4 there and how we might structure the first audits under T8. It will also give us a good test case for the standard incident and damage assessment process in T12.

I have now updated A1 with service cost estimates, digital usage indicators, and incident summaries for the candidate pilots, and I have refined the T6 shortlist. The proposed phase 1 list includes: one under occupied building with recurring service issues, one with strong digital engagement, one with known quality issues, and one relatively well performing property as a reference. The selection criteria are now: impact on occupancy and service issues, digital readiness, quality risk, and operational feasibility. Please confirm if you are comfortable with this mix for phase 1.

The updated mix looks balanced from a financial and operational standpoint. It gives us both improvement potential and a benchmark. I am comfortable using this list as the basis for the business case in A2 and the efficiency modelling in T11.

From the ICT and sustainability side, the list works well. Having at least one digitally engaged building and one with more challenges will give us a good spread for T3 and T7. I support using this as the phase 1 pilot set.

I am also comfortable with this mix. The property with known quality issues will be a good test for the checklist in A4 and the audit approach in T8, while the better performing one will help us see how the standards apply in a more stable context.

Given the feedback, I am comfortable approving this shortlist as our phase 1 pilot set under T6. The mix aligns with our need for both quick wins and learning. Let us record this as the agreed list of phase 1 pilot properties and services.

Thanks, I will mark the approved pilots clearly in A1 and in the T6 documentation, and I will inform the local teams. For the criteria, I suggest we keep the four we used here as the standard for later phases as well, unless we see a strong reason to adjust after the pilots.

I agree with keeping the same criteria for later phases: impact on occupancy and service issues, digital readiness, quality risk, and operational feasibility. That consistency will help when we compare results across phases and when we update A2 and the KPI dashboard in A5.

Let us then formalise those four criteria as our standard for prioritising properties beyond phase 1. We can revisit them after we see pilot results, but for now they will guide future selections. We should record this as our agreed prioritisation criteria.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate the green ICT roadmap and communication plan.

messages.text: I have drafted a first version of the green ICT roadmap in A3 for T3, focusing on tenant portals, energy monitoring, and digital communication. In parallel, I started a draft communication plan in A6 for T7, outlining key messages and channels for tenants and staff. The roadmap groups initiatives into three waves, with phase 1 aligned to the pilot properties we just approved under T6. Before we lock anything, I would like your input on two points: 1) which ICT initiatives we should include in phase 1, given operational and budget constraints, and 2) whether the communication approach in A6 feels realistic for your teams and tenants.

Looking at A3, the phase 1 list includes portal enhancements, basic energy dashboards, and digital notices. From an operations standpoint, portal enhancements and digital notices are manageable for the pilots, as long as we coordinate timing with local teams. The energy dashboards might require more coordination with facilities and suppliers, so I would prefer we limit that to one or two pilot buildings in phase 1. On A6, the messages are clear, but we need to be careful not to overwhelm tenants with too many changes at once.

From the financial and business case side, the initiatives in A3 look promising, but we need to be mindful of the budget envelope that will be set under T10. For phase 1, I would prioritise low dependency, low cost items that still show visible benefits, such as portal usability improvements and digital communication features. Energy monitoring can be piloted in a limited way, as suggested, so we can gather data for A2 without committing to large investments yet.

From a quality and audit perspective, the digital initiatives in A3 can help with consistency if we design them well. For example, digital notices and portal features can standardise how we communicate incidents and maintenance windows, which will support T12 later. However, we need to ensure that any new digital process is reflected in the checklist in A4 and that we can audit it during T8. On A6, I would suggest we include a short section on how we will inform tenants about any changes to incident reporting.

I like the structure of A3 and the way A6 links messages to specific initiatives. For phase 1, I want us to focus on a small set of ICT changes that are easy to explain to tenants and staff and that do not create support overload. Portal improvements and clearer digital notices fit that description. Energy monitoring is important for our sustainability story, but I agree we should start small. On communication, I want to be sure we have a simple narrative about why we are doing this and how it benefits tenants.

Understood. Based on your feedback, I propose that phase 1 under T3 includes: 1) portal usability and access improvements for all pilot properties, 2) standardised digital notices for maintenance and sustainability tips, and 3) a limited energy monitoring pilot in one or two buildings, focusing on simple dashboards rather than complex automation. I will adjust A3 accordingly. On A6, I can simplify the tenant messaging so that we introduce changes in stages rather than all at once.

That proposal works for operations. If we keep energy monitoring limited in phase 1, I can coordinate with the relevant site teams without stretching resources. For A6, I would like to see a clear timeline of when each tenant facing change will be communicated, so we can align with any local notices or meetings.

From a business case angle, that set of phase 1 initiatives is manageable and still gives us data and visible improvements. I will reflect these choices in A2 and in the assumptions for T11. It would be helpful if A3 clearly labels which items are in phase 1 versus later waves, so we can track them in the KPI dashboard in A5.

I support that selection. For quality, the digital notices and portal changes will be the most relevant in phase 1. Please make sure A6 includes a short explanation of how tenants should report issues through the portal or other channels, so we can align that with the standard process in T12 and the checklist in A4.

I have updated A3 to clearly mark the three phase 1 initiatives and moved the more complex items to later waves. In A6, I added a simple three month communication calendar for T7, with separate waves for portal changes, digital notices, and the energy monitoring pilot. Each wave includes draft messages for tenants and staff, and a note on who sends them.

The updated A3 and A6 look much clearer. The three month calendar for T7 is helpful, and the phase 1 initiatives are now easy to explain to site teams. I am comfortable rolling this out in the pilot properties, as long as we keep an eye on tenant feedback and adjust if needed.

I am aligned with the updated roadmap and communication plan. The phase 1 scope in A3 fits within the expected budget range for T10, and the staged communication in A6 should help manage expectations. I will integrate these into A2 and the KPI structure in A5.

From a quality standpoint, the updated A6 now clearly explains how tenants should use digital channels to report issues, which aligns with our plans for T12. I will make sure the checklist in A4 and the audit approach in T8 reflect these digital processes for the pilot properties.

Given the adjustments and the feedback, I propose we confirm the three phase 1 ICT initiatives as described in A3: portal usability and access improvements for all pilots, standardised digital notices, and a limited energy monitoring pilot in one or two buildings. This will be our agreed phase 1 ICT scope under T3.
Confirmed from my side. The phase 1 ICT scope is clear and workable for the pilot properties. We will coordinate locally to support the rollout.

Thanks all. On the communication plan in A6 for T7, can we also confirm that the three month calendar and the key messages are approved for the first rollout, so I can start preparing materials with the local teams?
From the housing side, I am comfortable with the communication calendar and key messages in A6. The sequencing works for our teams, and the content is clear for tenants and staff.
I am also aligned. The plan in A6 supports the broader narrative in A2 and should help manage expectations during the pilots.

With your confirmations, I am happy to approve the tenant and staff communication plan in A6 for the first rollout under T7. Let us record that as our agreed communication approach for the pilot phase.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on quality, compliance and audit approach for pilot properties.

messages.text: I have shared a draft of the Housing Quality and Compliance Checklist in A4 for T4, and I have also uploaded initial findings from two pilot style audits in A7 as part of T8. The checklist covers safety, service quality, and some sustainability criteria, and the pilot audits were run on two properties similar to our phase 1 pilots. I would like your feedback on three points: 1) whether the checklist in A4 is practical for your teams, 2) how we should prioritise remediation actions from A7, and 3) how to align this with the standard incident and damage assessment process we will define in T12.

Thanks for pulling this together. A4 is comprehensive, but I am a bit concerned about the time it will take site teams to complete the full checklist during busy periods. For the pilots, I suggest we keep all safety related items mandatory, but consider grouping some of the service quality and sustainability checks into a lighter version for routine visits. On A7, the findings around delayed responses to incidents match what we see on the ground, so we need to address that early.

From a business and governance perspective, A4 is a good foundation, but we should be clear about which items are critical for compliance and which are more about continuous improvement. That will help us prioritise remediation actions in A7 and manage costs. For T12, I would like to see a simple flow that links incident reporting, assessment, and follow up actions, so we can later connect it to KPIs in A5.

Looking at A4 and A7, I see a few points where digital tools from A3 and A6 could help. For example, we could use digital notices and portal messages to inform tenants about upcoming inspections or to follow up on incidents. For T12, it would be useful if the standard process includes a step where digital channels are used consistently, so we can track and audit communication as well.

From my side, I want to ensure that the checklist in A4 is robust enough to satisfy regulators and our own standards, but not so heavy that it becomes a barrier to consistent use. On remediation, we should focus first on any safety or legal compliance gaps in A7, then on issues that strongly affect tenant experience. For T12, I would like a clear and simple process that we can explain to the board and to tenant representatives.

That makes sense. I can adjust A4 so that safety items remain mandatory for every audit, while service quality and sustainability items are grouped into core and extended sections. For the pilots, we can use the full checklist during initial baseline audits under T8, and a lighter version for follow up visits. On A7, I will highlight the delayed incident responses as a priority area for remediation.

The split between mandatory safety items and core or extended sections sounds workable. For T12, I would like the standard incident and damage assessment process to reference the same categories as A4, so teams do not have to learn two different structures.

I will mark in A4 which items are critical for compliance and which are more about continuous improvement, and I will reflect that in the remediation plan derived from A7. For T12, I can draft a simple flow that starts with incident reporting, moves to assessment and classification, and ends with remediation and follow up, with clear responsibilities at each step.

When you draft the flow for T12, please include a point where digital channels are used to confirm to tenants that their incident has been received and to update them on progress. That will tie in nicely with A3 and A6 and will also give us data for future analysis.

Once the critical versus improvement items are marked in A4 and the remediation plan from A7 is clearer, I can estimate the cost and effort of addressing the main gaps and reflect that in A2 and T11. It will also help us decide how much of this we can tackle in the first year budget under T10.

I have now updated A4 with the split between mandatory safety items and core or extended sections, and I have tagged critical compliance items. In A7, I have grouped findings into three buckets: safety and legal compliance, tenant experience, and process efficiency. For remediation, I propose we prioritise safety and legal items first, then high impact tenant experience issues, and finally process improvements that can be scheduled over time.

The updated A4 and A7 structure works for operations. Prioritising safety and legal items first is non negotiable, and the tenant experience bucket will help us focus on the most visible issues in the pilots. I support this remediation order.
I am aligned with that prioritisation. It will also make it easier to phase remediation costs in the financial model in A2 and the efficiency work in T11.

From my side, the prioritisation also makes sense. For the tenant experience bucket, we can support some of the remediation actions with digital communication from A6, especially where we need to explain temporary disruptions or new processes.

I have also drafted the standard incident and damage assessment process for T12, aligning categories with A4 and including a step for digital confirmation to tenants as suggested. The flow is now: incident reported, initial triage and safety check, detailed assessment and classification, remediation planning, execution, and closure with tenant feedback. Responsibilities are mapped to site teams and central support.

The incident process flow for T12 looks clear and consistent with A4. My only request is that we include a simple escalation rule for cases where remediation is delayed beyond a certain threshold, so site teams know when to involve central support.

Good point. I will add an escalation step to T12 for cases where remediation exceeds agreed timelines, with clear thresholds and contacts. That will also help us track and report on overdue actions in future audits under T8.

Given the updates and your feedback, I propose we approve the checklist in A4, with the structure you described, as the standard quality and compliance checklist for the pilot properties under T4. This will be our reference for audits and for the incident process in T12.

On remediation priorities from A7, we will follow the order you proposed: first safety and legal compliance items, then high impact tenant experience issues, and finally process efficiency improvements. Let us record this as our agreed remediation priority order for the pilot audits under T8.

threads.thread_goal: Lock budget envelope, KPI dashboard and reporting cadence.

messages.text: I have shared an updated KPI dashboard mock up in A5 for T5, along with initial budget scenarios for the first year based on our current view of T2, T3, T4, T6 and T11. The dashboard focuses on occupancy, tenant satisfaction, service quality, sustainability indicators, and key financial metrics. The budget scenarios reflect different levels of investment in ICT, operations, and quality improvements. I would like your feedback on two things: 1) whether the KPI set and dashboard structure in A5 meet your needs, and 2) how comfortable you are with the proposed budget ranges and phasing for T10.

Looking at A5, the overall structure is clear. I appreciate the split between financial, operational, and sustainability metrics. For the board, I want to make sure we have a small set of headline KPIs that tell the story at a glance, with the option to drill down. On the budget scenarios for T10, I need to be confident that the first year spend is realistic given our broader commitments, and that we can show some early results within the first quarter.

From the housing side, the KPIs in A5 that matter most day to day are occupancy, turnaround time for vacant units, incident resolution time, and tenant satisfaction. The sustainability metrics are important too, but they will move more slowly. I would like to ensure that the dashboard allows us to see pilot properties separately from the rest of the portfolio, at least in the first year. On the budget, the operational improvement line looks tight, so we will need to be disciplined about prioritising actions from A7.

On the ICT and sustainability side, I am glad to see digital adoption and energy usage metrics in A5. For phase 1, we should keep the ICT related KPIs simple: portal usage, digital communication reach, and basic energy trends in the pilot buildings. More advanced metrics can come later. Regarding the budget scenarios, the ICT envelope in T10 looks reasonable for the phase 1 scope we agreed in A3, as long as we phase more complex items into later years.

From a quality and audit perspective, I would like to see at least one KPI in A5 that tracks audit completion rates and another that tracks closure of critical findings from A7. That will help ensure that T4, T8 and T12 are visible at the executive level. On the budget, the quality and audit line seems modest but workable if we focus on the pilots first and scale later.

Thanks for the feedback. I can adjust A5 so that we have a small set of headline KPIs at the top: overall occupancy, tenant satisfaction index, incident resolution time, a simple sustainability index, and net financial impact. The rest can sit in supporting sections. For the budget in T10, the current scenarios assume a moderate investment in ICT and a phased approach to operational and quality improvements, with most heavy spend in the second and third quarters.

I will configure A5 so that pilot properties can be viewed separately from the rest of the portfolio, at least for the first year. That will help us see the impact of T6 and related initiatives. On the operational budget, you are right that it is tight. The idea is to focus on high impact remediation actions from A7 and efficiency gains from T11 to fund some of the improvements.

For ICT metrics, I will keep the initial set in A5 to portal usage, digital communication reach, and basic energy trends in the pilot buildings, as you suggest. More advanced metrics can be added once T3 and T7 are more mature.
I will add two KPIs to A5: one for audit completion rate on pilot properties and one for closure rate of critical findings from A7. That will make T4, T8 and T12 more visible in the dashboard.

I have now updated A5 with the headline KPIs, pilot versus portfolio views, and the additional quality and ICT metrics. For T10, I propose we adopt the middle budget scenario: moderate ICT investment aligned with A3, focused operational remediation on the pilots, and a staged rollout of quality audits. This scenario balances ambition with our financial constraints and still allows us to show early results.

The updated A5 looks good from an operational standpoint. The pilot versus portfolio view will be very useful. I can work with my team to provide the data needed for the occupancy and incident metrics. The middle budget scenario for T10 seems realistic, as long as we keep a close eye on unplanned maintenance costs.

From the ICT and sustainability side, the middle budget scenario in T10 aligns with the phase 1 scope we agreed in A3. The ICT related KPIs in A5 are also manageable to track with the data we will have from T3 and T7.

I am comfortable with the added quality KPIs in A5 and the budget line for audits and remediation in the middle scenario. It should allow us to complete T4 and T8 for the pilots and start embedding T12 without overextending resources.

With your feedback, I am ready to confirm the KPI set and dashboard structure in A5 for executive reporting under T5. The headline KPIs and the ability to view pilots separately will work well for the board. Let us record this as our agreed KPI and dashboard structure.

On the budget, I propose we adopt the middle scenario you outlined in T10: moderate ICT investment aligned with A3, focused operational remediation on the pilots, and a phased rollout of quality audits. This will be our budget envelope and phasing for the first year of the initiative.

I will document the agreed KPI set and the budget scenario in A2 and T10, and I will update A5 accordingly. I will also propose a monthly reporting cadence for the dashboard, with a short written summary after each steering meeting.
Once the budget envelope is documented under T10, I will brief the housing teams on what is in scope for the first year and how we will track progress using the KPIs in A5.
